status: Discovery hypotheses and execution constraints, not return recommendations

portfolio_constraints.protocol_eligibility: At least 12 months old, at least $50m TVL and audited unless separately approved
portfolio_constraints.target_role: Stretch objective, not a discovery exclusion rule

mechanisms.name: Collateralized destination inventory replacement
mechanisms.economic_cause: Fragmented venue inventories and asynchronous settlement can leave prices apart. A collateralized destination loan can temporarily replace purchased inventory while its bridge transfer settles.
mechanisms.who_pays_and_earns: Trader may retain a venue spread; liquidity venues collect swap charges, block producers collect execution charges, lenders collect credit charges, bridge infrastructure may collect settlement costs. No net amount established.
mechanisms.recurrence_hypothesis: Liquidity shocks and inventory imbalances can recur; a historical instance does not establish durable accessible spreads after competition.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: Observed Ethereum WBTC bridge mint to Arbitrum WBTC, with WETH spent and native ETH received. Nominal token relation does not remove bridge/issuer/redemption risks.
lifecycle: Repay debt and reconcile remaining assets, fees and released collateral
mechanisms.financing: Persistent collateralized borrowing across separate transactions, not a same-transaction flash loan. Pre-existing collateral and liquidation buffer are unknown.
mechanisms.access_and_capital: Historical sample spends 50 WETH and uses additional unmeasured credit collateral. It is not a demonstrated $50k portfolio; do not linearly scale its result.
costs_and_risks: Borrow interest and collateral opportunity cost
mechanisms.observed_signal: Six public loan lifecycle witnesses on 2024-07-23; sale amount contradicts paper's summarized ETH gain.
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: Independently reconcile the six receipts and historical collateral/debt position, then determine whether any scaled notional can meet exposure/leverage limits after all charges.

mechanisms.name: Historically executable hedge during non-atomic settlement
mechanisms.economic_cause: Settlement latency creates exposure while a cross-venue spread is being closed. A genuine matching derivative might reduce common price risk, but its execution and carry consume spread.
mechanisms.who_pays_and_earns: Derivative counterparties exchange funding and basis; venues, lenders and settlement infrastructure collect fees. A hedge can lose on otherwise winning paths as well as offset losses.
mechanisms.recurrence_hypothesis: Price/settlement mismatch can recur; no identified actor-day or historical matching derivative is established for the reported GNO/ZGAP/DOS examples.
mechanisms.lifecycle: Unspecified until exact trades and historically listed matching instruments are identified. Entry and exit must both be executable at causal timestamps and realistic size.
mechanisms.financing: Margin, credit, funding timestamps, liquidation buffer and collateral overlap must be included; no assumption of free or continuously prorated funding.
mechanisms.access_and_capital: No venue, historical entitlement, book depth, effective fee tier or margin state identified.
mechanisms.observed_signal: None for reported 21-trade day. All required identification and original-time listing/depth fields remain null in candidate-input-manifest.json.
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: Recover exact actor, UTC day, all 21 transactions and token identities; then test original-time instrument existence before any hedge PnL computation.

mechanisms.name: Paid execution access as a constraint on ordinary cross-venue arbitrage
mechanisms.economic_cause: Scarce reliable inclusion and execution latency have an access price; gross venue differences need not remain with an entrant after access and failed-execution costs.
mechanisms.who_pays_and_earns: Traders pay access/intermediation and execution charges; sequencing/right owners or validators may capture much of gross value.
mechanisms.recurrence_hypothesis: Execution scarcity can persist, but this is a cost/entry gate, not evidence that purchasing access is profitable.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: Requires an independently identified legitimate cross-venue trade; none supplied by the access mechanism itself.

contract_context.basis: Reported in EMP-TIMEBOOST-2026 Appendix 0.A; not independently RPC-verified

mechanisms.lifecycle: Establish eligibility and full access cost, then evaluate ordinary trades without exploiting pending users or manipulating ordering.
mechanisms.financing: Auction deposits or intermediary billing can lock capital or add per-fill costs. Current entrant terms unknown.
mechanisms.access_and_capital: BAM Direct Bundle Ingest requires requesting access and whitelisting; observed Timeboost control is concentrated. No assumption of free universal direct access.
costs_and_risks: Off-chain payments missing from public PnL
mechanisms.observed_signal: Official 2026-10-13 BAM deployment report plus 2026 Timeboost empirical revision; neither measures this entrant's cross-chain net PnL.
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: Check actual entrant eligibility and total quoted access cost before assuming this execution path in any candidate economics.
